title: Wood floor cleaner
subtitle: A dilute vinegar and castile soap solution for sealed hardwood floors
excerpt: A dilute cleaning solution for sealed hardwood and laminate floors, a small amount of white vinegar, castile soap, and warm water. Applied with a barely damp mop. Not suitable for unsealed, oiled, or waxed wood. Makes one mop-bucket batch (enough for a medium room). Use immediately.
sourceNotes: Dilute white vinegar (5% acetic acid) for sealed hardwood: safe at heavy dilution (1-2 tbsp per 4 litres). Undiluted vinegar or repeated high-concentration use damages polyurethane sealants over time. Castile soap (potassium soap of olive/coconut oil) at very low concentration (a few drops) lifts oil-based residue without leaving a film. Essential oil for fragrance: optional; tea tree at 0.5% adds antimicrobial benefit. Laminate floors are sealed and can tolerate this solution. Unsealed, oiled, or waxed floors: water and vinegar will strip the finish or raise the grain, do not use.

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 mop bucket (approx. 4 litres, enough for one medium room)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mix to order. Vinegar solutions degrade with time and the essential oil dispersal drops once the solution cools. Mix fresh for each use.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Use immediately. Do not store, mix fresh for each cleaning session.

glossaryTerms.definition: A plant-oil-based soap (traditionally olive oil, now often a coconut-olive blend) available as a liquid concentrate. A few drops in water cut through greasy residue without leaving a film.

content.text: Wood floor cleaner is a dilute solution of white vinegar,

, and warm water for sealed hardwood and laminate floors. The mop head should be barely damp, excess water left standing damages wood floors regardless of the solution used. Not suitable for unsealed, oiled, or waxed wood. Mix fresh for each use; makes one bucket (enough for a medium room).

items.prepNote: 4 litres warm water; the dilution makes this safe for oiled/waxed wood floors
approx. 2 tbsp; or distilled white vinegar; cuts grease and deodorises
approx. 5 drops; use only a tiny amount to avoid soap film on floor
approx. 10 drops; antimicrobial; omit for lacquered floors

content.text: Fill the mop bucket with warm water. Add the vinegar, castile soap, and tea tree oil (if using). Stir briefly.
Dip the microfibre flat mop head and wring until almost dry, the mop head should feel only slightly damp, not wet.
Mop with the grain of the wood. Wring frequently. Do not let standing water pool on the floor.
No rinsing needed. The floor dries quickly at the concentration used here.

Sealed (polyurethane-finished) hardwood and laminate: suitable. Oiled wood floors: water and vinegar will strip or cloud the oil finish, use the cleaner recommended by your floor's oil manufacturer instead. Waxed floors: vinegar removes wax polish. Unsealed wood: any water will raise the grain over time.
